lede: Stuart ran one of the busiest front offices in the league — 113 adds, 115 winning claims, five trades — and ended with the team most shaped by its draft. Two-thirds of the category value came from players drafted in October, and the best of them, Jamal Murray at $28, added 0.71 a week. A 10–9 record, seventh seed, a 4–5 playoff loss to Fantastic 5, and a win in the fifth-place game.
profile: A guard team, and a pure one. Free-throw percentage won 18 of 21 matchups, first in the league at .835. Assists and steals at 71%, threes at 62%. The cost is two categories conceded almost every week: blocks 3–18 and rebounds 3–17–1. It is the mirror image of Brighton. Giving up two categories before tip-off means needing five of the remaining seven — which is exactly how a team that wins 4.6 a week finishes 10–9.
ledger: 97 of 189 categories, with a bye in week 21. The close weeks show the problem. Nine matchups came down to one category, and Masters went 4–5 in them, including the playoff loss to Fantastic 5. The early season was the high point: 8–1 over Ben's Need Some VC in week 2, and 6–3 or better in weeks 6 to 8.
draft: The top of the draft was the season. Jamal Murray at $28 was the best pick for the price: 0.71 categories a week, +0.27 over par. Donovan Mitchell at $41 added 0.68 (+0.16) and LaMelo Ball at $20 beat his price by +0.11. Austin Reaves at $30 was a wash, started in 12 of 19 weeks. Cason Wallace at $1 was the board's bargain, and it paid off. The misses were bigs and wings, which fits the profile. Kristaps Porzingis ($19, −0.20 against par) was traded on day 20, Coby White ($15, −0.17) on day 121, and Khris Middleton ($4, −0.20) never stuck.
production: Only a third of the value came from outside the draft. The most valuable additions came by trade: Payton Pritchard added +0.62 a week after arriving on day 97, and Alperen Sengun +0.38 over his 11 weeks. For all the claims, the in-season additions supplemented the drafted guards rather than replacing them.
trades: Five trades, all recovered, and a mixed record on both lenses. Day 12, Grayson Allen for Trae Young: good call, bad break. Young's line was worth more at the time (+0.09 expected), and he barely played, so it delivered −0.16 a week over 13 weeks. Day 20, Porzingis and Tari Eason for Sengun was the reverse: a poor call on the numbers (−0.45), rescued to +0.07. Day 93, Deandre Ayton for Naz Reid, was a good call that paid off (+0.10 over six weeks). Day 97, Sengun for Shaedon Sharpe and Pritchard, was the best call of the season (+0.51 expected). It paid off in the regular season (+0.10) and broke badly in the playoffs (−0.31). Day 121, Coby White and Mark Williams for Dillon Brooks, was a poor call, and it cost you (−0.34 expected, −0.14 delivered).
wire: The volume was enormous: 115 winning claims from 488 attempts, on a top bid of just $6, with $11 of FAAB left unspent. The return per move was mid-table: +0.08 categories a week against the player replaced, sixth of 14. The best moves came at the end of the season: Herbert Jones for Jordan Goodwin on day 126 (+0.60 a week) and Ace Bailey for Devin Carter on day 129 (+0.48), with Saddiq Bey on day 37 the best lasting one (+0.37 over six weeks).
bench: Thirty wasted player-days and 742 production on the bench — the most in the league. Week 13 accounts for four of the six biggest: LaMelo Ball 55 and Jimmy Butler 47 on day 87, Sengun 40 and Ayton 40 later that week, in a matchup lost 3–6. Ball appears three times in the top six. Some of that is a crowded roster with more starters than slots. But for a team living on five-of-seven weeks, 742 benched is the most avoidable number on this page.
last: The fifth-place game against The Infirmary, played properly: 50 starting slots set against 38, nine of nine on the last day, and a 6–3 win. Points 810 to 507, assists 190 to 87 — the guard build doing what it was built to do.
closing: The paradox of this season is that a manager this active had a team so decided by its draft. The guards bought in October — Murray, Mitchell, Ball — were the season. Everything after added movement more than value: the wire mid-table despite the volume, and the trades a coin toss between good calls that broke (Young, the Sengun sale in the playoffs) and poor ones. Two changes would matter most. Lineup attention first — the league-leading 742 benched is the cheapest improvement available. Then a decision on the bigs: conceding blocks and rebounds every week makes every matchup a five-of-seven, and that is how nine one-category weeks ended 4–5. The guard core is good enough. One real centre held all season would have changed the math.
